flow.costOfRevenueNote: What it cost to run the cloud platform and deliver services — hosting, support and implementation.
flow.grossProfitNote: Revenue left after the direct cost of running the platform — 78.9% of revenue, down from 80.0% a year ago.
flow.netIncomeNote: The bottom line: $460M kept as profit, 14.9% of revenue — GAAP profit is held down because $470M of stock-based pay sits inside the costs above.
flow.operatingIncomeNote: A $451M operating profit — a 14.6% margin, up from $332M a year ago. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding stock-based pay and other items, it was $953M.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to big enterprises — the largest running cost, up from $923M a year ago.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the AI platform, including Now Assist and agentic AI; up from $606M a year ago.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day; up from $222M a year ago.

flow.otherIncomeNote: $115M of interest income on the cash pile, less $11M of other expense, net.
flow.revenueNote: Money from software subscriptions and professional services.
flow.taxNote: A $95M tax provision on $555M of pre-tax income — a 17.1% effective rate.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to the nearest cent, so the rounded rows sum to $14.89 of profit per $100, a cent below the rounded $14.90. Stock-based compensation of $470M is spread across the cost and expense rows above — it is a real cost to shareholders through dilution, even though no cash leaves the bank.
footerNote: Subscription revenue up 19% to $3.01B; net income $460M.

kpis.label: Current remaining performance obligations
kpis.note: +22% YoY; revenue contracted for the next 12 months

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation of $470M (up from $422M a year ago) is the largest non-GAAP add-back and the main reason GAAP operating income of $451M trails non-GAAP operating income of $953M. It is excluded from non-GAAP results, but it is a real cost — it dilutes existing shareholders.
Business combination and other related costs of $11M, excluded from non-GAAP results.
Amortization of purchased intangibles of $21M, excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $104M is $115M of interest income on ServiceNow's cash and investments, less $11M of other expense, net.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: The AI platform, sold by subscription — 97% of all revenue; up 19% YoY. Subscription gross profit was $2,444M, an 81.5% margin.

segments.name: Professional services & other
segments.note: Implementation and consulting help for customers; up 4.5% YoY. Gross profit was a $7M loss — this work is nearly break-even by design.

takeaways.text: Subscription revenue grew 19% to $3.01B — 97% of all revenue — with 72 deals over $1M in net new annual contract value in the quarter. The customer base keeps moving upmarket: 508 customers now spend more than $5M a year, up about 20%.
takeaways.title: Subscriptions did the growing

takeaways.text: Current remaining performance obligations — revenue already contracted for the next 12 months — grew 22% to $10.31B, and total remaining obligations reached $22.1B, up 25%. The contracted backlog is growing faster than revenue, which is what funds the next quarters.
takeaways.title: The backlog is growing faster than sales

takeaways.text: GAAP operating income was $451M, a 14.6% margin, while non-GAAP operating income was $953M at a 30.9% margin. The $502M gap is mostly $470M of stock-based pay. Free cash flow was $1,477M, a 47.8% margin, and ServiceNow bought back $298M of its own stock.
takeaways.title: The GAAP profit is less than half the adjusted one

verdict: ServiceNow grew revenue 18.5% to $3.09 billion, with subscription sales up 19% and $10.3 billion of revenue already contracted for the next twelve months.
